Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : BM3606 : Laser and Fiber Optics { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module-I: Introduction to Optics, Laser, Photonics, Biophotonics, Fiber Optics. The Laser source, design, and development, types of lasers. Spontaneous and stimulated emission, Population inversion Pumping methods and levels of pumping Characteristics-Monochromaticity, Coherence, Directionality Polarization of Light and Laser emission.
Module-II: Laser Types- Solid state, Ruby, Nd:YAG, Gas lasers: Helium-Neon, Argon and Co2. Lasers in ophthalmology, Dermatology, Dentistry, Urology, Otolaryngology, Tissue welding, Laser in Biomedical Applications.
Module-III: Introduction to Photonics, Biophotonics, Principle and propagation of light in optical fibers, Numerical aperture and Acceptance angle, Active and passive fiber sensors- Endoscope.
Module-IV: Optical Properties of Tissues-Scattering, Absorption, Refractive Index, Light transport inside the tissue, Light interaction with tissues, Optothermal interaction.
Module-V: Interferometry, Types of Interferometry, Michelson Interferometry, Mach-Zehnder Interferometry, Optical Holography-Wave fronts, interference patterns, the principle of the hologram, optical hologram, applications.

Course Objective

1 .

To introduce fundamental principles of Optics, Lasers, and Fiber Optics commonly used in biomedical research.
2 .

To familiarize the basic Optoelectronic systems, techniques, and considerations for the development of biomedical devices.
3 .

To understand the role of Light and Lens in Bio-medical instrument development.
4 .

To get hands-on experience in various Opto-Biomedical Instrumentations for familiarity with the implementation and working principles of the instruments.

Course Outcome

1 .

After completing the course, the students will be able to:
1. Have a thorough understanding of the fundamental concepts and techniques used in Optics, Lasers, and Fiber Optics.
2. The ability to understand, Optoelectronic systems, techniques, and considerations for the development of biomedical devices.
3. Ability to identify the role of Light and Lens in Bio-medical instruments.
4. To develop skills to realize, build, and troubleshoot Biomedical Instruments and get hands-on experience in various Opto-Biomedical Instrumentations for familiarity with the implementation and working principles of the instruments.
5. To understand the practical circumstance of Laser and Fiber Optics in Biomedical devices.

Essential Reading

1 .

Markolf H.Niemz, Laser-Tissue Interaction Fundamentals and Applications, Springer

2 .

Leon Goldman, Lasers in Medicine, Springer-Verlag

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Leon Goldman, The Biomedical laser Technology and Clinical Applications, Springer-Verlag

2 .

Paras N. Prasad, Introduction to Biophotonics, John Wiley and Sons

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CE3001 : Estimation and Construction Management { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Estimation (8 hours):
Introduction to estimation, Units of measurement, Types of estimation, Methods of approximate estimation, Detailed estimation (Long wall/short wall method and Centre line method), Estimation of earthwork, sanitary & water supply works, irrigation works and road works.

Module 2 :

Reinforcement quantity estimation (4 hours):
Basis of Bar Bending Schedule (BBS), BBS of beam, column, one way & two way slabs and isolated foundation.

Module 3 :

Specification and Valuation (4 hours):
General specification and detailed specification for different building items & structural works, and Methods of valuation of a building.
Module 4 :

Analysis of rates (4 hours):
Analysis of rates for earthwork, brickwork, reinforced cement concrete work and plastering.
Module 5 :

Contracts & Tendering (8 hours):
Types of construction contract, Elements of a contract document, Different methods of carrying out work contract, Measurement book, and Method of tendering.
Module 6 :

Construction project management (8 hours):
Project planning, Project scheduling, Project controlling, Bar charts & Milestone charts, Development of network, Network analysis, Network rules, Work breakdown structure, Elements of PERT and CPM and Project crashing.

Course Objective

1 .

At the end of the course, the students are expected to understand the principles and techniques for estimating the quantities and construction costs of various structures, including buildings, sanitary and water supply works, irrigation works, and roadworks.
2 .

At the end of the course, the students are expected to calculate the rates of different essential items for a construction project.
3 .

At the end of the course, the students are expected to write detailed contract specifications for materials, equipment, and construction methodologies for various construction projects.
4 .

At the end of the course, the students are expected to demonstrate their ability to use various project management tools for planning, scheduling, and controlling time and costs on different infrastructure projects.

Course Outcome

1 .

Estimate the quantities of materials and costs for various construction projects, including buildings, irrigation works, and road works.
2 .

Perform rate analysis for the various construction projects.
3 .

Prepare contract documents for a given project.
4 .

Apply various material & equipment management techniques to ensure quality control.
5 .

Optimize the time and cost of a construction project using various project management tools.

Essential Reading

1 .

B. N. Dutta, Estimating and costing in civil engineering: Theory and practice, CBS Publishers & Distributors Pvt Ltd , 28th revised edition

2 .

B. Sengupta and H. Guha, Construction Management and Planning, McGraw Hill Education , Standard Edition

Supplementary Reading

M. Chakraborti, Estimating, Costing, Specification and valuation in Civil Engineering, Chakraborti publisher , 29th revised and enlarged edition

2 .

P. S. Gahlot & B. M. Dhir, Construction planning and management, New Age International Pvt. Ltd. , 2nd edition

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CH2172 : Fluid Dynamics Laboratory { 0-0-3 / 2}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

1. Determine the flow regime with the help of Reynolds apparatus.
2. Verify Bernoulli’s equation experimentally.
3. Compare the theoretical and experimental pressure drop in a fluidized bed and determine the minimum fluidization velocity by using Ergun Equation.
4. Study the Reciprocating pump characteristics.
5. Study the Centrifugal pump characteristics.
6. Find the permeability coefficient of a given medium using Darcy’s law.
7. Determine the drag coefficient of a spherical particle and plot the CD vs Reynolds number curve.
8. Determine the friction factor for fluid flow in a helical coil.
9. Find the coefficient of pitot tube and draw the velocity profile.
10. Determine the friction losses for flow in a straight pipe of different diameters.
11. Determine the discharge coefficient of the Venturimeter, Orifice meter and calibrate the Rotameter.
12. Verify Ergun’s Equation for pressure drop in a packed bed.

Course Objective

1 .

The basic aim is to perform practical studies on various types of fluid flow systems and determine or estimate various characteristic parameters associated them

Course Outcome

1 .

(i) Characterize fluid flow pattern and study energy conservation in fluid flow.
(ii) Apply Bernoulli’s theorem in a fluid flow network.
(iii) Analyze the flow rates, velocity and pressure in the given flow system.
(iv) Handle preliminary instruments like pressure gauge and U- tube manometer, Venturimeter, Orifice meter, Rotameter, pitot tube and pumps (Centrifugal and reciprocating pump).
(v) Analyses the variation in pressure drop with fluid velocity for flow in a fluidized and packed bed

Essential Reading

1 .

Sarbjit Singh, Experiments in Fluid Mechanics, PHI Learning Private Ltd. , 2nd Ed., 2012

2 .

W.L. McCabe, J.C. Smith, P. Harriot, Unit Operations of Chemical Engineering, McGraw-Hill Publication , 2014

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CY7106 : Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Electromagnetic radiations: Types of molecular energy and molecular spectroscopy(1 hour). NMR Spectroscopy: Basic principles (2 hours), Chemical shift (2 hours), Spin-Spin Coupling (2 hours), Coupling Constant (2 hours), NOE, 13C NMR (6 hours), 19F, 31P NMR (2 hours), DEPT NMR (2 hour), heteronuclear coupling (2 hour), Pulse NMR spectroscopy and techniques (2 hours), relaxation time and their importance (2 hours), 2D NMR spectroscopy: COSY, NOESY, HMQC, HMBC (7 hours) Problem involving these techniques for structural determination and other applications (8 hours).

Course Objective

1 .

To introduce NMR Spectroscopy, a vital method of characterization of organic molecules.
2 .

Problem solving by NMR spectroscopy
3 .

To give details of different nuclei/atom characterisation by NMR Spectroscopy.
4 .

To train students for phrmaceutical jobs and research in any field dealing with organic molecules.

Course Outcome

1 .

1) The students will able to understand the basic concept of NMR spectroscopy used for the analysis of organic compounds.
2) Detailed discussions on principles, instrumentation and applications of these techniques will be carried out.
3) Information about application and importance of 2D NMR spectroscopic methods, would help in complex molecule characterization.
4) The students would learn the elucidation of structures from the NMR spectrum (Both 1D and 2D)
5) Different aspects of NMR spectroscopy , besides structure elucidation, would be detailed.

2 .

J. Mohan, Organic Spectroscopy, Narosa Publishing House

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : EE6250 : Flexible AC Transmission Systems { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module1:
Introduction to FACTS: FACTS Concept and general system consideration: Transmission Interconnections, Flow of Power in AC Systems, Loading capability, Power flow and Dynamic Stability Considerations of a transmission interconnection, Relative Importance of Controllable Parameters, Basic types of FACTS Controller. .
4 Hours
Module2:
Shunt Compensation : Static Shunt Compensators: Objectives of Shunt Compensation, Methods of Controllable VAR Generation, Static VAR Compensators: SVC and STATCOM, Comparison between STATCOM and SVC,
12 Hours
Module3:
Series Compensation: Static Series Compensators: Objectives of Series Compensation, Variable Impedance type Series Compensators, Switching Converter type Series Compensators, External Control for Series Reactive Compensators
10 Hours
Module4:
Angle Compensation: Static Voltage and Phase angle Regulators: Objective of Voltage and phase angle regulators, Approaches to Thyristor-controlled voltage and phase angle regulators, switching converter-based voltage and phase angle regulators, Hybrid phase angle regulators.
4 Hours
Module 5:
Combined Compensation: Combined Compensators: Unified power flow controller (UPFC) and Interline power flow controller (IPFC)
6 Hours

Course Objective

1 .

Understand the concepts of Flexible Power Transmission
2 .

Understand Ideal shunt and practical shunt compensation using Thyristors (TCR) and Bridge Converters (STATCOM)
3 .

Understand the concepts of ideal series, practical series using Thyristors (TCSC) and Converters (SSSC)
4 .

Understand the concepts of Transient Stability Enhancement and Power Oscillation Damping using shunt and series compensation

Course Outcome

1 .

CO1: Classify the FACTS devices into Thyristor based and Converter based.
CO2: Insight into the Transient Stability Enhancement, Power Oscillation Damping, Transient Stability Margin.
CO3: Understanding the voltage and the current waveforms with respect to thyristors and the converters for both shunt and series compensation.
CO4: Understanding the dynamics of stability of voltage regulation using SVC and STATCOM with the variation of line reactance.
CO5: Conceptual understanding of independently controlling the active and the reactive power through circular control regions.
CO6: Insight into the sub synchronous oscillation damping and resonance for series compensated transmission lines. .

Essential Reading

1 .

N.G.Hingorani & L.Gyugyi, Understanding FACTS: Concepts and Technology of Flexible AC Transmission Systems,, IEEE Press, 1999 , It is nice for essential reading and should be used as the base text book

2 .

Y. H. Song and A. T. Johns, Flexible AC Transmission Systems, , IET, 1999. , It is a good text book

Supplementary Reading

1 .

1. X.P. Zang, C. Rehtanz and B. Pal, Flexible AC Transmission Systems: Modeling and Control, Birkhauser, 2006. , It is fine for supplementary reading

2 .

Acha, Esquivel, Prez and Camacho, Modeling and simulation in power networks, Wiley India Private Limited, 2012 , It is a decent text book

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : PA4611 : Advanced Building Services { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module I: Introduction to the HVAC system in buildings: Important concepts and pre-requisite knowledge of HVAC – Thermal comfort and IAQ, Psychrometric chart and the comfort zone, Givoni-bioclimatic chart, Refrigeration cycle, Thermal properties of the built element, evaluation of heat flow in a building, Concept of a ‘Ton of Refrigeration’.
Module II: HVAC systems in buildings:Dx type-Window AC and block diagram for Window AC, Working of a Thermostat, Split AC and block diagram, Standalone-Packaged Unit and block diagram, VRV type of HVAC and block diagram
Centralized HVAC system with block diagram (Hydronic type) – Centralized HVAC system and its components – Water cooled condenser, Air-cooled condenser, working of an AHU with block diagram, Working mechanism of Variable Air Volume System.
Module III: Cooling Load and Mechanical Ventilation (Volumetric Air Flow Rate) calculations: Cooling Load Calculations – Formulas and concepts for estimation of External Loads (Sensible and Latent Heat Sources), Formulas and concepts for estimation of Internal Loads (Sensible and Latent Heat Sources), Total heat load in a space
Volumetric Air Flow Rate Calculations – Concept of CFM and its calculation for various occupancies as per NBC-2016, Selection of appropriate HVAC systems as per the heat load, and volumetric flow rate calculations,
Space Planning for HVAC Systems – Plant Room size, AHU room size, and equipment planning based on heat load or tonnage and CFM calculations as per the National Building Code of India and various manufacturers' catalogues available, Air Distribution System design- Selection of Diffusers and Grilles, Duct size calculation, Single line block diagram for HVAC layouts.
Module-IV: Mechanical Transportation System in buildings: Definition and types of mechanical transportation systems/ Elevators, Escalators, and Travelators. Working mechanism and components of Lifts-Traction Lifts, Hydraulic Lifts, Machine Roomless Lifts (MRL) Lift lobby design, The working mechanism of Escalator and Travelators – Design considerations, Location, Sizes, and Components
Module-V: Traffic Analysis calculations for Lift Design: Lift design metrics/ Performance Criteria for Lift Design: Average Waiting Interval (AWI) Calculations, Round Trip Time (RTT) calculations, and Lift Handling Capacity calculations.
Integration of lifts in a building: No of lifts, size and capacity, operation sequence, arrangement of lifts as per the National Building Code of India.
Lift Design Considerations for High-Rise Buildings: Lift Zoning System and Sky Lobby System.

Course Objective

1 .

To understand the fundamentals of HVAC systems in a building, their various types, and analyse their integration with building design.
2 .

To understand the fundamentals of various mechanized vertical transportation systems in a building and analyse their integration with building design

Course Outcome

1 .

1. Ability to apply knowledge of mechanical services (HVAC and mechanized transportation systems) in the design of buildings.
2. Ability to determine the cooling load and mechanical ventilation requirements of space to select an appropriate HVAC system for the desired thermal comfort and indoor air quality requirements of the building concerned.
3. Ability to determine the occupancy loads and perform Traffic Analysis to design, select, and integrate appropriate mechanized vertical transportation systems with the architectural design of buildings with reference to the National Building Code of India.
4. Ability to understand layouts and drawings related to Mechanical Services in a building and integrate the same with architectural drawings.

Essential Reading

1 .

BIS (2016)., National Building Code of India., Bureau of Indian Standards

2 .

Hall, F., & Greeno, R. (2007)., Building Services Handbook. (4th Edition)., Oxford, England.

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Wujek, J. B., & Dagostino, F. R. (2010)., Mechanical and electrical systems in architecture, engineering, and construction., Pearson Education.

2 .

McQuiston, F. C., Parker, J. D., Spitler, J. D., & Taherian, H. (2024)., Heating, ventilating, and Air Conditioning: Analysis and Design., Wiley.
